grants.Program Focus:
OPENING SUMMARY — WEEK OF SEPTEMBER 7 – 11, 2026

Energy / Rural Generation and Storage: USDA RUS Powering Affordable Reliable Technology (PART) Energy Program (RUS-PART-2026) — roughly $410 million in budget authority supporting loans of $1,000,000–$100,000,000 with up to 40% forgiveness, for hydropower, geothermal, biomass, and storage serving majority-rural areas. Loan, not a grant.

Letters of Interest due 11:59 a.m. ET, October 9, 2026 — reviewed on a rolling basis in the order received, so earlier is better.

Agriculture / Value-Added: USDA RBCS Agriculture Innovation Center Demonstration Program (RBCS-2026-AIC), $2,500,000 across roughly 3 awards, $600,000–$1,000,000; one-third match required. Due January 31, 2027, submitted by email rather than Grants.gov.

Agriculture / Seafood Processing: USDA RBCS Meat and Poultry Processing Expansion Program Phase 3, Round 2 — Invasive, Wild-Caught Catfish (RD-RBS-26-03-MPPEP), $6,000,000 across roughly 6 awards, $50,000 to the lesser of $2,000,000 or 80% of project cost; 20% cost share. Due December 7, 2026. No rural-area requirement; applicant must already process seafood commercially and its state must have an invasive-species plan that names catfish.

California State Opportunities: CalRecycle Legacy Disposal Site Abatement Partial Grant (SWC 109) — $1,500,000, up to $750,000 per applicant, 50% match, public entities only. Due September 16, 2026 — one week after posting.

CAL FIRE Forest Legacy Program Capacity and Project Development 2026 — $500,000, $50,000–$150,000 per award across 4–10 awards, no match. Due-diligence and capacity funding for land trusts and conservation nonprofits developing future working-forest easements. Due September 30, 2026.

CalRecycle Illegal Disposal Site Abatement Grant (SWC 108) — $1,000,000, up to $500,000 per award, no match, public entities only. Due October 16, 2026.

CalRecycle Recycled Glass Processing Incentive Grant (FY 2026–27) — $8,782,179, $1,000,000–$4,000,000 per award, 100% match. Certified beneficiating processors only. Due October 22, 2026; questions close October 6.

Watch List / Upcoming: DOL VETS Homeless Veterans’ Reintegration Program family (FOA-VETS-27-01), forecast — $12,000,000 across 31 awards, $150,000–$500,000, no match. Estimated posting January 29, 2027; estimated due date March 17, 2027. Puerto Rico, the U.S. Virgin Islands, and Guam are the only eligible territories.

DWR Watershed Resilience Program, Proposition 4 — about $152 million across two upcoming solicitations (~$60 million Conservation Implementation; ~$92 million Planning+). Draft guidelines were issued Sept. 10, 2026.

grants.Description: USDA Rural Utilities Service — Powering Affordable Reliable Technology (PART) Energy Program
grants.Opportunity #: RUS-PART-2026; Assistance Listing 10.757 (Powering Affordable Reliable Technology Energy Program). Grants.gov opportunity 363396. Federal Register notice published August 4, 2026.
grants.Agency / Funder: USDA Rural Development — Rural Utilities Service (RUS), Electric Program. PART Help Desk SM.RD.RUS.PART-Questions@usda.gov; RUS General Field Representatives by state.
grants.Total Funding:
Approximately $410 million in budget authority under Inflation Reduction Act § 22001, available through September 30, 2031. The Simpler.Grants.gov listing shows about 100 expected awards.

Budget authority converts to a larger lending volume, and the LOI Guide gives two different figures: approximately $1.1 billion in loans (executive summary) and approximately $815 million available to lend (Section I.E).
grants.Award Range: $1,000,000 minimum to $100,000,000 maximum, inclusive of the forgivable portion. Combined PACE, PART, and any other IRA § 22001 awards to one entity may not exceed $100 million. Up to 40% loan forgiveness. Interest at the municipal rate; term up to 35 years.
grants.Eligible Applicants:
Operating utilities organized as for-profits, nonprofits, state or local governments, federally recognized Tribes (including wholly owned arms and instrumentalities), Alaska Native Corporations, distribution and generation-and-transmission electric cooperatives, or certified electric utilities. One LOI per entity; one award per applicant. An entity already approved under PACE or New ERA may not apply for the same project.

Service-area screen. At least 50% of the area where the power is consumed — not where the project sits — must be rural (outside any city or town over 20,000; current and former RUS borrowers’ territories are deemed rural). The Administrator may waive the threshold for excessive energy burdens or severe economic conditions.
grants.Deadline:
Letters of Interest due 11:59 a.m. ET, October 9, 2026 — a noon deadline, not midnight — through Grants.gov only (no paper, fax, or email). The LOI window opened September 8, 2026.

LOIs are reviewed on a rolling basis in the order received, so earlier submission matters. The Administrator may also weigh geographic diversity, Substantially Underserved Trust Area (SUTA) status, and Opportunity Zone investment. Invited applicants then have 60 days to file a full loan application; awards anticipated September 2026 through December 2027.
grants.Program Focus:
Financing for new renewable generation — limited this round to hydropower, geothermal, and biomass — and new energy storage charged by any Section 317 source, which the RD page says includes wind and solar. Also eligible: new or upgraded lines, transmission and distribution, microgrids, transformers, interconnection costs, pre-application costs (7 CFR part 1767), and interest during construction.

Excluded: merchant power, self-generation, consumer-owned behind-the-meter projects, purchase of existing generation or storage, and technology that is not commercially available. Construction may not begin before the NOFO publication date or before written RUS environmental clearance.

Loan forgiveness requires showing ratepayer benefit through a long-range financial forecast and NPV analysis. The LOI package is the SF-424, the PART LOI form, WGS84 service-area and project-location shapefiles for each project, and three years of financial statements. Build America, Buy America applies to non-federal entities; foreign ownership must be disclosed.
grants.Funding Instrument:
Loan, not a grant. Project Loans are secured by project assets and revenue, require collateral assignment of the PPA, and disburse only after commercial operation begins. System Loans are limited to operating utilities, require a perfected senior lien on all assets, and may disburse during construction.

Forgiveness applies only after the project is complete and all award conditions are met.
grants.Cost Share / Match: Project Loans finance up to 75% of total capitalized cost; the borrower must put in at least 25% cash equity (not debt-derived) and maintain it for the life of the loan, plus one-year O&M and debt-service reserves. Tax credits or direct payments may count toward equity at the Administrator’s discretion, and up to 100% financing is possible for SUTA areas. System Loans may cover up to 100%.
grants.Primary Sector: Rural Electric Utilities; Hydropower; Geothermal; Biomass Power; Energy Storage; Microgrids and Transmission; Inflation Reduction Act
grants.Link to NOFO: PART program page (USDA RD); PART on Simpler.Grants.gov; PART 2026 NOFO (PDF); LOI Guide (PDF); PART FAQs (PDF); Federal Register notice (PDF); Grants.gov listing
grants.Posting Date: LOI window opened and Simpler.Grants.gov listing posted September 8, 2026

grants.Description: USDA Rural Business-Cooperative Service — Agriculture Innovation Center Demonstration Program (FY2026)
grants.Agency / Funder: USDA Rural Development — Rural Business-Cooperative Service. Program staff mppep@usda.gov. No-cost application help is available through the USDA AMS Meat and Poultry Processing Capacity Technical Assistance (MPPTA) network.
grants.Total Funding: $6,000,000 (FY2024, FY2025, and FY2026 funds); approximately 6 awards. RBCS may increase the total at its discretion.
grants.Award Range: $50,000 minimum. Maximum is the lesser of $2,000,000 or 80% of total project costs. Period of performance up to 48 months.
grants.Eligible Applicants: Eligible applicants include for-profit and nonprofit entities, producer-owned Cooperatives and corporations, certified benefit corporations, Tribes and Tribal Entities, State or local government entities, and other business types (regardless of legal structure). Private entities must be Independently Owned and Operated, and all entities must be Domestically Owned. Additionally, the applicant’s Processing facilities must be physically located and operating in the United States (U.S.) or its territories. There is no rural area requirement for the program. Applicants must also: (1) Currently process Seafood or Wild-Caught Catfish for commercial markets and have been in business for more than a year; (2) Operate or plan to operate under a Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) grant of inspection from USDA to process Invasive, Wild-Caught Catfish subject to the Federal Meat Inspection Act (FMIA); (3) Plan to increase processing capacity for Invasive, Wild-Caught Catfish, at their existing Facility; and (4) Have a State Aquatic Nuisance Species, or Invasive Species, management plan that specifically identifies catfish as an Invasive or Aquatic Nuisance Species in the State where the Facility operates.
grants.Deadline: December 7, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, through Grants.gov only. Opened September 8, 2026. RBCS recommends submitting at least two weeks early. Anticipated announcement and award February 8, 2027.
grants.Program Focus:
Increase processing capacity and throughput for invasive, wild-caught catfish, with the parallel aim of reducing invasive populations. Eligible activities: new facility construction or purchase of an inoperable facility (including real estate); mobile slaughter and processing units; modernizing or expanding existing facilities, including wastewater structures; cutting, skinning, de-scaling, and de-boning equipment; automation; food-safety, emissions, and water-efficiency upgrades; composting and packaging equipment; HACCP plan revisions; and staffing or training tied to the project.

Not allowable: vehicles (other than mobile units), planning, feasibility or R&D, technical assistance, indirect costs, subawards, and pre-award costs.

Scoring is out of 115 points: alignment and marine impact (20), market development and fisher opportunities (20), financial viability (20), technical merit (20), labor and personnel (10), community support (10, requires letters from qualifying leaders), plus up to 15 discretionary points for geographic and species diversity, prioritizing apex predators. Minimum fundable score is 50. Narrative limit 20 pages.
grants.Funding Instrument: Grant, through a Financial Assistance Agreement (Form RD 4280-2). Disbursement by single payment at completion, reimbursement with a 10% holdback, or advance.
grants.Cost Share / Match: At least 20% of total project cost, verified at award. Third-party in-kind contributions allowed under 2 CFR 200.306.
grants.Primary Sector: Seafood Processing; Invasive Species Management; Food Supply Chain Resilience; Food Safety (FSIS / HACCP); Fisheries and Watermen; Rural Economic Development
grants.Link to NOFO: MPPEP Phase 3 Round 2 on Simpler.Grants.gov; NOFO (PDF); USDA RD program page; Application Template (DOCX); Application Checklist (PDF)
grants.Posting Date: NOFO published September 8, 2026; USDA announcement September 9, 2026

grants.Description: CalRecycle — Legacy Disposal Site Abatement Partial Grant Program (Cycle SWC 109, FY 2026–27)
grants.Opportunity #: California Grants Portal ID 191106. Status Active; opened September 8, 2026.
grants.Agency / Funder: CalRecycle, Beverage Container Recycling program. Contact Danbaki Johnson, (916) 658-4778, danbaki.johnson@calrecycle.ca.gov. Written questions to BevContainerGrants@calrecycle.ca.gov.
grants.Total Funding: $8,782,179 — the $4,000,000 annual allocation plus $4,782,179 remaining from Cycle 2.
grants.Eligible Applicants:
Must be a current certified beneficiating processor and either (a) a private for-profit entity qualified to do business and in good standing in California, or (b) a nonprofit (other than a private school) organized under 501(c)(3), (c)(4), (c)(6), or (c)(10).

Subsidiaries, divisions, and affiliates count as one entity; a business is affiliated if an owner holds 40% or more of another applicant. Projects must be located in California.
grants.Deadline: October 22, 2026, through CalRecycle’s Grants Management System. Questions close October 6, 2026. Secondary due date November 12, 2026 for authorization documents (resolution or letter of commitment) and an Environmentally Preferable Purchasing and Practices policy, if not submitted with the application. Awards expected January 2027.
grants.Program Focus:
Increase the supply of furnace-ready glass cullet used to make new glass beverage containers in California. Projects must demonstrate the ability to expand furnace-ready cullet processing in the state, and within 12 months of award the grantee must show CalRecycle how much additional cullet the grant produced. Authorized under Public Resources Code § 14543 (SB 1013).

The portal lists a performance period of January 19, 2027 – April 1, 2029, while CalRecycle’s cycle page sets the final report and final payment request deadline at April 4, 2028. Resolve before building a project schedule.
grants.Funding Instrument: Competitive state grant; advances and reimbursements.
grants.Cost Share / Match: 100% match — equal to or greater than the grant amount. Other CalRecycle funding cannot be used as match.
grants.Primary Sector: Glass Recycling; Beverage Container Recycling; Circular Manufacturing; Materials Processing; Recycling Infrastructure
grants.Link to Solicitation: Recycled Glass on the California Grants Portal; CalRecycle Notice of Funds Available; Application Guidelines and Instructions; Q&A page; Grants Management System

grants.Description: U.S. Department of Labor, VETS — Homeless Veterans’ Reintegration Program (HVRP), Incarcerated Veterans’ Transition Program (IVTP), and Homeless Women Veterans’ and Homeless Veterans with Children Reintegration Grant Program (FY2027 Forecast)
grants.Opportunity #: No solicitation number yet. DWR plans two Proposition 4 solicitations: Conservation Implementation and Watershed Resilience Planning+.
grants.Agency / Funder:
California Department of Water Resources — Financial Assistance Branch, (916) 651-9613.

The contact email on DWR’s page is inconsistent: it displays FinancialAssistance@water.ca.gov but links to dwr_irwm@water.ca.gov.
grants.Total Funding: Approximately $153 million across the two solicitations: The Watershed Resilience Grant Program will be administered as two separate solicitations. Each solicitation has specific requirements and selection processes. Program schedules can be found at the website shown in the Foreword. • Conservation Implementation Solicitation – Approximately $60.1 million will be awarded for projects that increase water conservation in agricultural or urban areas. • Planning + Solicitation – Approximately $93 million will be awarded to support the development of new Watershed Resilience Plans or to update existing Watershed Resilience Plans and fund the highest priority implementable project(s) identified through this planning process.
grants.Eligible Applicants:
Eligible applicants are public and local agencies, special districts, joint powers authorities, 501(c)(3) nonprofits, public utilities, local publicly owned utilities, mutual water companies, federally recognized Tribes, and California Tribes on the Native American Heritage Commission's consultation list. Partner organizations that carry out individual projects under the lead applicant must also be eligible. If the lead applicant is ineligible, the whole application fails; if a partner is ineligible, only that partner's project is dropped. Applicants must also pass the standard state water-grant compliance checks: groundwater management and SGMA, groundwater monitoring, stormwater resource plans, urban and agricultural water management plans, water metering, and surface-water diversion reporting.

Eligible projects include water recycling and potable reuse, conservation and efficiency, storage and groundwater recharge, regional conveyance, watershed restoration (including wildfire-risk reduction), conjunctive use, and desalination. Projects on private property must show a measurable public benefit, such as acre-feet of water saved, and record a 30-year deed restriction. Landscape rebates and fallowing are not eligible..
grants.Deadline: Draft Guidelines and Proposal Solicitation Package were released Sept. 10. Public comment workshops: October 12, 2026, 10 a.m.–12 p.m. (Tribal only) and October 22, 2026, 1–3 p.m. Planning+ draft Guidelines expected this winter, with concept proposals in late 2027.
grants.Program Focus:
Successor to the Integrated Regional Water Management (IRWM) program, with more emphasis on climate vulnerability assessment, adaptation planning, and watershed-scale collaboration across water supply, flood, groundwater, water quality, forest and fire, ecosystem, and land-use sectors.

Conservation Implementation funds capital projects with a water-conservation benefit. Planning+ funds a Watershed Resilience Plan and then implementation of its top-priority projects. The program builds on five 2024 pilots, including the Sonoma County Water Agency’s Russian River watershed effort.
grants.Funding Instrument: Competitive state grant, Proposition 4 bond funds.
grants.Primary Sector: Watershed Resilience; Water Conservation; Climate Adaptation; Integrated Regional Water Management; Flood and Groundwater Management; Proposition 4 Climate Bond
